reasons: Direction is correctly assessed: Section 7.2 obliges Customer to disclose and match third-party offers for Vendor's benefit, which is the burdening direction the rule targets, not a Vendor-granted MFN.

The clause fails the fallback — no defined product, no 12-month limit, no reasonable-comparison carve-outs — and is an open-ended duty to match better terms, i.e. walk-away territory, so 'deviation' is the right status.

The redline (full deletion of p0026) matches the redline guidance ('delete the obligation on Customer'); the paragraph consists solely of the offending obligation, so deletion is the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position, and no Vendor-granted MFN is lost.
Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, prefixed correctly, states what changed and why, and offers a constructive alternative (MFN in our favour) rather than lecturing.
Only minor point: the cross-reference to Section 12.3 is not in the supplied paragraphs, but it is presented as supporting context and is not load-bearing for the finding.
